title: Simulation Through the Halting Step
statement: Let $M$ be an $m$-tape machine and $R$ a $k$-tape machine whose states are in $S\oplus\mathrm{Unit}$. Suppose $E$ maps configurations of $M$ to configurations with state set $S$ and preserves their optional state components. Assume that whenever a configuration $d$ of $M$ is not halted, one step of $R$ from the state-renamed image of $d$ is the return encoding of $E$ applied to the result of one step of $M$. Let $c$ be a nonhalted initial configuration and let $T$ be a natural number such that every configuration of $M$ at times $t<T$ is nonhalted, while its configuration at time $T$ is halted. Then for every $t<T$, the run of $R$ from the state-renamed image of $E(c)$ equals the state-renamed image of $E$ of the configuration of $M$ at time $t$; at time $T$ it equals the configuration obtained from $E$ of $M$'s time-$T$ configuration by setting its state to the right-hand summand; and at every time $t<T$, its state is not that right-hand summand.
hypotheses_covered: machines M and R with the stated tape counts and state types
configuration map E preserves optional states
one-step simulation condition for every nonhalted configuration
all M configurations at times t<T are nonhalted
M is halted at time T
